title: TCS New York City Marathon — Watch the Race
claims: The majority of the course is open to spectators from mile 3 to mile 26.
There is no spectator viewing at the start or on the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge.
Fourth Avenue in Brooklyn is recommended for miles 2 to 4, and Fourth Avenue and Flatbush Avenue for mile 8.
Williamsburg and Greenpoint in Brooklyn are recommended for miles 10 to 13, before runners head toward the Pulaski Bridge.
The Pulaski Bridge at mile 13.1 connects Brooklyn to Queens and is closed to spectators.
First Avenue in Manhattan is recommended for miles 16 to 18, and East Harlem for miles 18 to 20.
Fifth Avenue from East 90th Street to East 105th Street is recommended for miles 23 to 24.
The race finishes at 67th Street on West Drive in Central Park.

Spectators can access the final approach through grandstand seating or a standing spectator area inside Central Park from Columbus Circle to the south end of the grandstands, about 500 feet before the finish.
There is no spectator access north of the grandstands in Central Park.
Spectators are not allowed on any of the bridges on the course.
The best way for spectators to get around is the subway, with mta.info checked before travel.
